mouse tissues, the frequency of mcm5h2U was <10% of cytoplasmic
tRNAs bearing mcm5s2U (Fig. 3b, d), and τm5h2U was detected in only a
few percent of mitochondrial tRNAs with τm5s2U (Fig. 3h, j). However,
the abundance of h2U derivatives varies in different cell types.
Approximately 15% of tRNALys in HeLa cells contained mcm5h2U,
whereas little was detected in A549 and T24 cells (Supplementary
Fig. 3). Since h2U derivatives can be generated by oxidative desul-
furation in vitro55,56, it is highly likely that they are chemically produced
in cells by reactive oxygen species generated under oxidative stress
conditions. Nevertheless, enzymatic formation of h2U derivatives
cannot be ruled out. In vitro oxidative desulfuration of s2U derivatives
yields both h2U and uridine derivatives; however, since the desulfura-
tion mechanism in cells remains unclear, the ratio in which these two
types of products are formed is unknown. While h²U derivatives are
likely to represent a form of damaged RNA, the uridine derivatives
generated by desulfuration may be re-thiolated back to 2-thiouridine,
suggesting that this is a reversible modiﬁcation. Understanding the
mechanisms underlying the differing frequencies of h2U derivatives in
various cells and tissues is intriguing. The frequency of h²U is likely
determined by multiple factors, including the cellular oxidative stress
response, redox balance, and the degradation of h²U-modiﬁed tRNAs.
Because s2U derivatives playa crucial role in codon-speciﬁc translation,
our discovery suggests that tRNA s2U modiﬁcation serves as a sensor to
monitor intracellular oxidative states to regulate codon-speciﬁc
translation (Fig. 8). In fact, although we quantiﬁed h2U derivatives
under various oxidative stress conditions, we have not yet identiﬁed
any conditions that reproducibly increase h2U levels (Supplementary
Data 4). Sierant et al.59 likewise detected mcm5h2U in yeast and human
cultured cells and analyzed its behavior under oxidative stress using
calibration curves der

captions.label: Fig. 1
captions.caption:
Fig. 1 | Desulfuration of 2-thiouridine derivatives found in tRNA anticodons.
a The 5-methyl-2-thiouridine derivative (xm5s2U) is present at the ﬁrst position (34)
of tRNA anticodons. mcm5s2U and τm5s2U are found in eukaryotic cytoplasmic
tRNAs and animal mitochondrial tRNAs, respectively. mnm5s2U and cmnm5s2U
occur in bacterial cytoplasmic tRNAs. s2U is an intermediate of xm5s2U. b Reaction
scheme for oxidative desulfuration of xm5s2U in tRNA. 5-methyl-4-pyrimidinone
derivative (xm5h2U) and 5-methyluridine derivatives (xm5U) are generated by
in vitro oxidation and desulfuration of xm5s2U. This study only focused on xm5h2U.
c LC-MS nucleoside analyses of mouse total tRNA (top panels), in vitro oxidized
total tRNA (middle panels), and co-injection of both tRNAs (bottom panels) with UV
traces (254 nm, left panels), mass chromatograms for mcm5h2U (m/z 301, center
panels) and m1I (m/z 283, right panels). The relative abundance of each peak is
normalized against m1I abundance. d LC-MS nucleoside analyses of pig mito-
chondrial tRNALys (top panels), in vitro oxidized tRNALys (middle panels), and co-
injection of both tRNAs (bottom panels) with UV traces (254 nm, left panels), mass
chromatograms for τm5h2U (m/z 366, center panels) and m1A (m/z 282, right
panels). The relative abundance of each peak was normalized against m1A abun-
dance. Collision-induced dissociation (CID) spectra of mcm5h2U (e) and τm5h2U (f).

captions.label: Fig. 2
captions.caption:
Fig. 2 | Spike-in experiment with tracer tRNA. a Scheme of the spike-in experi-
ment with E. coli tRNAGln1 as a tracer. b Status of tRNA modiﬁcations in the tracer
tRNA before and after spike-in experiment. Extracted ion chromatograms (XICs)
show the indicated negative ions of RNase T1-digested fragments containing
modiﬁed U34. Sequences of detected fragments, with their molecular weights and
charge states, are displayed on the right. The relative modiﬁcation frequencies (%)
indicated in chromatograms were calculated from the peak height ratios of RNA
fragments with different modiﬁcations. A non-speciﬁc peak is asterisked. c CID
spectrum of the cmnm5h2U-containing fragment of E. coli tRNAGln1. d Frequencies of
cmnm5h2U and other uridine derivatives before and after spike-in experiments with
technical triplicates. Results are means ± standard deviation. Source data are pro-
vided as a Source data ﬁle.

captions.label: Fig. 3
captions.caption:
Fig. 3 | Detection of h2U derivatives in cytoplasmic and mitochondrial tRNAs.
Status of wobble modiﬁcations in mouse cytoplasmic tRNAs for Lys (a) and Gln (c),
and mitochondrial tRNAs for Lys (g) and Glu (i). XICs show the indicated negative
ions of RNase T1-digested fragments containing modiﬁed U34. Sequences of
detected fragments, with their molecular weights and charge states, are displayed
on the right. The relative modiﬁcation frequencies (%) indicated in chromatograms
were calculated from the peak height ratios of RNA fragments with different
modiﬁcations. Frequencies of h2U derivatives and other uridine derivatives with
technical replicates of mouse cytoplasmic tRNAs for Lys (b, n = 6) and Gln (d, n = 3),
and mitochondrial tRNAs for Lys (h, n = 2) and Glu (j, n = 5). Results are means ±
standard deviation. Source data are provided as a Source data ﬁle. CID spectra of
h2U-containing fragments of mouse cytoplasmic tRNAs for Lys (e) and Gln (f), and
mitochondrial tRNAs for Lys (k) and Glu (l).

captions.label: Fig. 4
captions.caption:
Fig. 4 | Desulfuration of tRNA modiﬁcation affects translation efﬁciency.
a Schematic diagram of HCV-IRES mRNAs of Rluc (upper picture) and mutant HiBiT
(lower picture) for human cell-free translation. b Luciferase activities of Rluc (left
bars) and mutant HiBiT (right bars) translated in vitro with either desulfurized or
untreated total tRNA. Results are means ± standard deviation from four indepen-
dent experiments. ***p < 0.001 (p = 0.00007, 95% CI = 248051–399017,
t(5.39) = 10.78, Cohen’s d = 7.62). n.s., not signiﬁcant (p = 0.566, 95%
CI = −186481–118851, t(3.80) = −0.63, Cohen’s d = −0.44). Unpaired two-tailed
Welch’s t-test. Source data are provided as a Source data ﬁle. c Western blotting of
HA-tagged Rluc with an anti-HA antibody. His-tagged eEF1A and eEF1Bγ were
blotted with an anti-His antibody as loading controls. Source data are provided as a
Source data ﬁle. d Scheme for polysome fraction preparation from HEK293T cells.
The free RNA fraction in the supernatant of the sucrose cushion is indicated. e SDG
proﬁling of crude ribosome from HEK293T cells. The polysome fraction is indi-
cated. f LC-MS nucleoside analyses of total RNA (left panels), free RNA (middle
panels), and polysomal RNA (right panels) from HEK293T cells. Mass chromato-
grams represent proton adducts of mcm5s2U (m/z 333, upper panels), mcm5h2U (m/
z 301, middle panels), and m1I (m/z 283, lower panels). The relative peak intensity is
normalized against mcm5s2U intensity in each analysis. g CID spectrum of mcm5h2U
in polysomal RNA. The base-related ion (BH2
+) is indicated.

captions.label: Fig. 5
captions.caption:
Fig. 5 | Desulfuration of tRNA modiﬁcation affects aminoacylation. Aminoacy-
lation of desulfurized (blue dotted lines) and untreated (black lines) total tRNAs for
Thr (a), Arg (b), Gln (c), Glu (d) and Lys (e). Results are means ± standard deviation
from three independent experiments. *p < 0.05 (c: p = 0.0337, 95% CI = 3.20–31.83,
t(2.11) = 5.00, Cohen’s d = 4.08; d: p = 0.0486, 95% CI = 0.14–23.84, t(2.83) = 3.34,
Cohen’s d = 2.72). ** p < 0.01 (e: p = 0.0035, 95% CI = 28.13–66.32, t(3.30) = 7.49,
Cohen’s d = 6.11). n.s., not signiﬁcant (a: p = 0.9877, 95% CI = −42.01–41.58,
t(3.4) = −0.02, Cohen’s d = −0.01; b: p = 0.4668, 95% CI = −12.06–7.07,
t(3.03) = −0.83, Cohen’s d = −0.68). Unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-test. Source data
are provided as a Source data ﬁle.

captions.label: Fig. 6
captions.caption:
Fig. 6 | Desulfuration of tRNALys affects codon recognition. Ribosomal A-site
tRNA-binding experiments performed for AAA (a) and AAG (b) codons with
desulfurized (blue dotted lines) and untreated (black lines) tRNALys. Data were
normalized against non-speciﬁc binding to the UUC codon. Results are means ±
standard deviation from three independent experiments. ** p < 0.01 (a: p = 0.0048,
95% CI = 0.1686–0.3355, t(2.20) = 11.91, Cohen’s d = 9.72; b: p = 0.0037, 95%
CI = 0.0914–0.1999, t(2.89) = 8.73, Cohen’s d = 7.13), Unpaired two-tailed Welch’s
t-test. Source data are provided as a Source data ﬁle.

captions.label: Fig. 8
captions.caption:
Fig. 8 | Proposed mechanism of translational regulation mediated by desul-
furized tRNA modiﬁcation. Under oxidative stress conditions, mcm5s2U34 mod-
iﬁcation of cytoplasmic tRNAs for Lys, Gln, Glu, and Arg undergoes desulfuration,
yielding mcm5h2U34. mcm5h2U34 decreases the aminoacylation efﬁciency of
tRNALys, tRNAGln, and tRNAGlu, and also impairscodon recognition atthe A-site on the
ribosome. As a result, codon-speciﬁc translation efﬁciency is negatively regulated.
